title: A Sigil for the Choir
premise: Sebastian Eriksen, a mercenary whose god of oaths has gone silent, has survived by hiding his gift among the smuggler roads of the Thornfell mountains. When the crown's witch-hunt burns through the passes, he learns that his estranged daughter Wren sold her soul to the court beneath the mountain to buy his safety—and the sale is final at the winter solstice. Gathering a ragged choir of other marked outcasts, Sebastian descends into the under-court to steal her soul back, discovering that his silent god never abandoned him but was imprisoned there, its voice harvested by the court's judges. In the climax Sebastian shatters the sigil that binds both god and souls, restoring his daughter at the cost of his own memories of her; in the end, Wren leads the freed choir home while Sebastian, remembering nothing, chooses to walk beside her anyway.
about_author: Cyrus Okonkwo is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing oral histories in mountain communities before turning to fiction full-time. He writes fantasy about faith, family, and the people justice forgets, and lives somewhere above the snow line with an opinionated dog.

chapters.title: The Silent Tithe
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Guiding a smuggler caravan through Thornfell, Sebastian quietly uses his gift to read a bridge's failing oath-stone and reroutes the party, hiding the act from everyone. He prays to his silent god out of habit and receives nothing. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence—the routine of a man who has made invisibility his religion.

chapters.title: Proclamation at Greyford
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the lowland town of Greyford, criers announce the crown's hunt: all gifted must register or burn. Sebastian watches a neighbor—a gentle hedge-healer—dragged away, and recognizes the lead hunter as an old comrade, Captain Ilse Varga. Emotional beat: fear curdling into guilt; his years of silence bought him nothing but complicity.

chapters.title: What Wren Sold
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A dying fence tells Sebastian that his daughter Wren, whom he abandoned years ago, traded her soul to the court beneath the mountain to shield him from an old bounty. The transaction completes at solstice—three weeks away. Emotional beat: devastation and self-recrimination; the debt he never knew she paid.

chapters.title: Wren, Below
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (first appearance). Beneath the mountain, Wren serves in the court's choir of half-souled servants, her memories thinning like frost. She remembers loving her father but not why. The Magistrate-Judges promise her soul will 'harmonize' at solstice. Emotional beat: quiet dread and stubborn hope as she hides a stolen shard of memory in a song.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Road
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Fleeing Greyford, Sebastian seeks Maren Ostvik, the healer's mentor, a blind woman who maps magic by sound. She agrees to guide him below—if he gathers others like them, because no one steals from the court alone. Emotional beat: reluctant first step toward community; belonging offered as strategy before it becomes need.

chapters.title: A Choir of Strays
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sebastian recruits three outcasts: Tam, a boy whose gift animates the dead; Odile, a forger whose sigils lie beautifully; and Brannoc, a disgraced priest still hearing echoes of the silent god. Each carries a warrant or a wound. Emotional beat: wary fellowship forming around shared danger, humor flickering at the edges.

chapters.title: Ilse Varga's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The huntress interrogates prisoners and finds Sebastian's name flagged in an old ledger—not for his gift, but for a massacre he was framed for years ago. Her faith in the crown's justice wobbles when the evidence doesn't match her memory of him. Emotional beat: doubt planted; the antagonist revealed as a believer, not a monster.

chapters.title: The Pass of Broken Oaths
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The company crosses a pass where the god's old covenant stones have been shattered. Brannoc hears fragments in the rubble: the god didn't fall silent—it was taken. Varga's hunters ambush them; Tam raises a dead mule to block the road, revealing his gift publicly. Emotional beat: the group's secret is spent; they are fugitives now, together.

chapters.title: Songs Under Stone
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers her hidden memory-shard inside the choir's ritual song and realizes the Judges harvest not just souls but the god's voice itself. She begins teaching the choir altered verses—small sabotages. Emotional beat: agency awakening; grief transmuted into quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. To forge court credentials for the descent, Odile trades a forgery to a corrupt magistrate who demands her sigil-hand as payment after. She agrees, telling no one. Emotional beat: sacrifice foreshadowed; the theme of justice outside the law embodied in a con artist's honor code.

chapters.title: The Gate That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the mountain's sealed gate, Maren reads its memory aloud: it opens only to a name spoken by someone who loves the person entering. Wren's childhood nickname, learned from the fence's letters, turns the lock. Emotional beat: love as literal key; Sebastian confronting how little he knows of his own daughter.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The company enters the under-mountain: bone-white halls where sound behaves strangely and every echo returns slightly changed. Brannoc's faith, long dead, stirs—he can feel the god nearby, muffled. Emotional beat: awe and terror; a lapsed priest feeling grace again in the worst possible place.

chapters.title: The Choir Recognizes Its Own
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren meets the infiltrators posing as soul-clerks and doesn't recognize her father—but his voice snags something in her song. She covers for their mistake before the Judges notice, then follows them secretly. Emotional beat: recognition without memory; blood answering blood across the void the sale carved.

chapters.title: Judgment Deferred
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Caught by a Judge, Sebastian is shown the court's logic: souls are currency, the god's voice is law, and order requires the harvest. The Judge offers Wren's freedom if Sebastian surrenders his own memories as raw material. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy; the cost of the rescue made explicit.

chapters.title: Varga Descends
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Varga, following the fugitives, finds the burned village records proving Sebastian's frame-up—and learns her superiors knew. Ordered to execute rather than investigate, she stalls, then descends alone. Emotional beat: the law's servant discovering the law is rotten; allegiance shifting from crown to conscience.

chapters.title: The Vault of Voices
chapters.summary: Alternating Sebastian and Wren. Father and daughter reunite in the vault where the god's voice is kept in ten thousand sealed jars, Wren's soul-sigil among them. She remembers him only as a story she once loved. They plan the theft: Odile's forged sigil, Tam's dead, Brannoc's hymn. Emotional beat: reunion without recognition—love persisting past memory, the book's thematic heart.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Preparations strain the group: Odile's debt comes due early, Tam falters raising enough dead, Maren warns the vault's silence will deafen her guidance. Wren volunteers to sing the corrupted choir-song as their opening. Emotional beat: dread and resolve braided together; each character paying forward what they owe the others.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Sigil
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The heist erupts. Odile's forgery fails under scrutiny; Varga arrives mid-chaos and, choosing sides, cuts down the pursuing guards. Sebastian reaches Wren's sigil but cannot crack it—until he pours his own memories of her into it as fuel, shattering it and freeing her soul. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice as the truest form of belonging.

chapters.title: The God Unmuzzled
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. With the sigil broken, the vault jars split open and the god's voice floods the under-court, collapsing the Judges' authority—law built on stolen speech dissolves into noise. The god speaks Sebastian's name, and offers to restore what he gave. It asks what he wants remembered. Emotional beat: catharsis and terrible choice; grace arriving with a price tag.

chapters.title: What He Chose to Forget
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian asks the god to restore Wren fully—even if his memories of her are the payment. He wakes on the mountainside knowing he loves someone he cannot picture. Wren, whole, finds him and introduces herself. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; identity as choice rather than recollection.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Up
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The freed choir, the outcasts, and a deserter named Varga climb toward daylight. Wren tells her father stories of himself—correcting them when they're wrong, keeping them when they're kind. The god's voice hums in the stones again, taking oaths freely given. Emotional beat: warmth earned; community rebuilt from the rescued.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Choir
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue. Months later, the group shelters refugees from the crumbling hunt in a rebuilt waystation. Sebastian carves a new sigil—not an oath of ownership but an invitation—into the door. Wren adds a verse. He still can't remember her childhood, but he's learning her present. Emotional beat: quiet hope; belonging chosen daily, memory be damned.
